scenes.headline: How Xiaomi's released RL environments turn work into reward
scenes.sub: The open kit behind MiMo-V2.6: tasks, containers, and the programs that grade them
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Kestrel! Xiaomi released the training environments behind its latest model. Here's how a task becomes a reward.

scenes.label: The idea
scenes.text: Every task ships with the program that grades it: hidden tests, a crash matcher, a rubric judge, a screenshot ranking or a music scorer.
scenes.say: Every task ships with the program that grades it. The model learns to raise that number, so the grader is the real specification.

steps.say: An agent gets a business brief and a workspace of documents.
A sidecar serves mock enterprise systems, each a tool server over a small database.
Afterwards a verifier reads the answer and the databases, and a language model judges each rubric item, pass or fail.
The items become one reward. Most are judged by that model, and you choose the model.
The report draws how these offices were built: real files and software mocks, filled in by agents and checked for consistency.
Then agents explore each one and write tasks with rubrics.

scenes.title: Five graders, five ideas of reward

items.text: Hidden tests arrive after the agent
items.say: Code: hidden tests arrive after the episode. Exit zero scores one.

items.text: Crash must land in the function
items.say: Cyber: the crash must land in the named function.

items.text: A rubric, mostly judged by LLM
items.say: General: a weighted rubric of pass or fail items.
Web dev: a vision model ranks all eight screenshots at once.
Music: the score is compared with human music. The brief is never read.

parts.say: The trainer grades a group of rollouts for one prompt.
Each is scored against the group's average. A constant cancels, and a group that ties teaches nothing.

scenes.title: Tasks per domain, counted
scenes.say: Counted from the files: seven thousand seven hundred and eighty tasks, in about forty-seven hundred environments.

scenes.text: The graders are readable, and they decide what gets learned: two need a judge you choose, and music ignores the brief.
scenes.say: The graders are readable, and they decide what gets learned. Two need a judge you choose.

recap: Every task ships with its own grader
The trainer learns from differences within a group
Judges and validation splits: bring your own
scenes.say: To recap: a grader per task, learning from differences, and a judge you bring yourself.
